newsitem.title: GERMANY: AOL to start "autumn offensive" in Germany.
newsitem.headline: AOL to start "autumn offensive" in Germany.

text.p: America Online and its European partner Bertelsmann AG said Tuesday they would launch an "Autumn offensive" adding new content and services to their online service to attract new subscribers.
Jan Buettner, managing director of AOL Germany, said the German-language version of AOL's new software would be available in November.

"We have grown much faster than initially thought and we are preparing ourselves for an autumn offensive to broaden our base," Buettner told reporters at the CeBIT Home consumer electronics fair here.

Later this year the company will offer high-speed digital ISDN access to its service, which will allow faster download times over normal telephone wires, and will expand online banking services to include Germany's biggest banks.
AOL has 200,000 subscribers in Europe, with around 150,000 of that total in Germany alone. Buettner would give no financial information about the service.
Thomas Middelhoff, Bertelsmann board member, said this week the service would break even in Bertelsmann's 1997/98 business year, two years ahead of schedule.
AOL's main pan-European competitor, CompuServe Corp., has over 800,000 subscribers in Europe, of which 270,000 are in Germany.
The biggest German online service, phone giant Deutsche Telekom's T-Online, has 1.2 million subscribers in Germany but is not available outside Germany.
Telekom and German publisher Axel Springer Verlag are planning to take a combined stake in AOL Germany of 25 percent, Bertelsmann New Media president Bernd Schiphorst said.
The deal, announced last November, will be concluded soon, with AOL taking a stake in T-Online. Details over the size of the equity swap have not been made public.
Andreas von Blottnitz, an AOL Germany director, said Vereinsbank would offer online banking on AOL.

In the next six weeks users will be able to check German stock prices within AOL and later this year the company will unveil a "virtual travel office" with last minute booking services and price comparisons of over 100 travel agencies.

The German version of AOL, which is accessible to all worldwide AOL members, will also launch a section called City Info, which is a list of German cities on the World Wide Web, the popular graphical part of the global Internet.
